plans.note: Section 21 is the full liability regime: 21.1 mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; 21.2 consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-ins; 21.3 defines Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP infringement) and preserves fee obligations; 21.4 savings language. Check cap adequacy and carve-out completeness before concluding; note also that insurance (18.2) states it does not limit liability.

Vendor IP indemnity at 20.1 and conduct/data/law indemnity at 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity at 20.3 (test whether it stays narrow — unmodified Customer material and Customer's unlawful use, with Vendor Technology/combination carve-outs); 20.4 procedure and settlement consent; 20.5 infringement remedies (cross-referenced by termination right in 9.3). Confirm indemnities sit outside the cap via 21.3.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to develop, buy, sell, or compete and disclaims non-compete/MFN/volume/no-hire commitments — beneficial to us, do not flag. Scan for any competing restriction elsewhere; the only restraint-type term found is the exclusivity language in Section 2.2 (first instance), which is handled under EXCLUSIVITY, so avoid double-flagging the same term here.

Section 2.2 (first of two provisions numbered 2.2) makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the whole term — a direct hit on this rule and inconsistent with 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment). Note the internal conflict when proposing deletion; do not confuse with the second sec-2.2-2 (order of precedence).

Section 7.2 (first of two provisions numbered 7.2) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms offered to any other technology supplier — MFN running against us, wrong direction under this rule. It also contradicts 12.3's disclaimer of any most-favoured-customer commitment. sec-7.2-2 is the unrelated invoicing clause.

Section 12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out — assess against the narrow, time-limited fallback. 12.3's general-recruitment language is in tension and supports our position.

Section 9 contains only for-cause exits (material breach 9.1, insolvency 9.2, Customer's special-cause rights 9.3) plus 9.5 on severability of Order Forms; 27.3 gives a force-majeure exit and 8.2 a non-renewal route. No convenience termination right for Customer appears anywhere, and equally no Vendor convenience right — likely missing; confirm across Sections 8–11 before concluding.

Section 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on 180 days' advance notice — test the notice window against the playbook's maximum. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, which is favourable; any missing renewal reminder mechanic is a rationale note, not a separate deviation.

28.1 selects New York law and disapplies the CISG; 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County state/federal courts with an injunctive-relief carve-out; 28.3 adds a pre-suit executive escalation that does not delay urgent relief. New York is an accepted jurisdiction and litigation (not foreign arbitration) is specified — likely compliant.

24.1 gives Customer free assignment to Affiliates and successors; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment/change of control and bars assignment to our competitors; 24.3 is the residual consent provision; 24.4 blocks Vendor from terminating, repricing, or degrading on our change of control. 13.3 permits transfer of licence rights consistent with Section 24. Direction favours us — verify no hidden Vendor exit right.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP with only a limited processing right to Vendor; 14.2 assigns Deliverables to Customer on creation subject to payment; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology but routes it through the perpetual licence in 13.2; 14.4 bars joint ownership and limits feedback use. Check definitions 1.3/1.4/1.8 for carve-outs (telemetry exclusion, unaided-memory know-how) and 15.1's no-model-training restriction.

13.1 grants a worldwide, non-exclusive subscription right extending to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; 13.2 gives a perpetual, irrevocable, paid-up licence for delivered/embedded Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to a material uncured breach after notice and cure; 13.4 sets use restrictions with lawful-reverse-engineering and security-testing carve-outs. Confirm no at-will revocation remains.

Section 22.1 lets Vendor audit at any time, without notice, with direct remote access to our systems and records — fails notice, frequency and off-site expectations. Note the conflict with 22.2, which bars direct system access and allocates costs to Vendor absent a >5% underpayment, and with 22.3 (findings are our Confidential Information); Section 23 (records/assurance) may hold related text.

Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency — uncapped, one-way, and squarely against the rule's direction. No offsetting service credits to us appear; relief for Vendor delay should instead run through schedule relief. Cross-check 21.2/21.3 on whether this exposure sits outside the liability cap.

19.1 professional/conformity warranty; 19.2 ninety-day Deliverable warranty running from the later of delivery or acceptance plus a term-long hosted Services warranty; 19.3 malicious code, legal compliance, no functionality degradation, open-source protection; 19.4 repair/re-perform then terminate-and-refund remedy that is expressly non-exclusive for IP, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 mutual disclaimer preserving express warranties. Acceptance mechanics in 6.1–6.2 are the related remedy path.

Section 18.1 sets CGL 1M/2M, workers' compensation, employer's liability 1M, professional E&O 2M and cyber/privacy 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers insurer quality, primacy, certificates, cancellation notice, and confirms insurance does not cap Vendor liability. Compare limits against playbook minimums given Vendor hosts Customer Data.

Section 2.1 states no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining a further Order Form is not a breach or shortfall; 12.3 repeats the absence of a minimum-volume commitment; 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges. Favourable to us — confirm no take-or-pay hides in the Fees or exclusivity provisions (sec-2.2) before treating as compliant.

Section 11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance at expiring Order Form rates with continued service levels; 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a documented machine-readable format and bars withholding for fee disputes; 11.3 covers certified secure deletion. Section 10.1–10.2 add post-termination deliverable handover and refunds; 16.5 defers to Sections 11 and 15 for Customer Data.
